briefs.summary: On November 9, Apple's stock rose 2.4% to a record close of $350.69, making the company worth about $5.1 trillion, more than Nvidia or Microsoft. It happened on the S&P 500's best day since April, and China's internet regulator also listed Apple Intelligence (Apple's AI features) as approved for iPads and Macs in China. briefs.summary: On November 10, JPMorgan was named a lead bank for the upcoming IPO (a company's first sale of stock to the public) of AI company Anthropic, handling sales to everyday investors. briefs.headline: Exxon signs a first-step deal to look at returning to Venezuela
briefs.summary: On November 9, Exxon signed a memorandum of understanding (a non-binding first agreement) with Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA to study new oil projects there. Venezuela took over Exxon's oil projects in 2007, and Exxon was awarded $1.6 billion plus interest in 2014, but that fight is still not settled. Exxon called the deal a meaningful first step but said it needs stable rules and good returns before it invests, and a final contract would still be needed. The same day, oil prices fell about 6% to their lowest since August, and Exxon's stock slipped about 0.3% to around $165.
bull: Venezuela has some of the biggest oil reserves in the world, and the deal could open a door to new oil for Exxon.
Exxon earned $4.23 per share last quarter, up from $3.52 the quarter before.
It plans to buy back $20 billion of its own shares in 2027, about 3% of the company.
bear: The Venezuela deal is not binding, and Exxon has not said which projects it might invest in.
Venezuela still has not paid the $1.6 billion award from when it took Exxon's projects in 2007.
Oil prices dropped about 22% from their October 30 high, and lower oil prices usually mean lower profits for Exxon.
briefs.nextEvent: Exxon's next dividend of $1.07 per share is paid on December 10, 2026

briefs.headline: J&J backs new cancer and depression treatments after good bipolar drug results
briefs.summary: On November 12, Johnson & Johnson said it will invest in Francis Medical, which makes a small-procedure device for prostate cancer, and led a $100 million funding round for Delix Therapeutics, which is working on new depression medicines. The stock rose about 1.3% that day. Two days earlier, J&J said its drug Caplyta helped adults with bipolar I disorder in a big final-stage test, with 43.9% of patients improving by half or more versus 23.7% on a fake pill. The stock dipped 1.25% to about $277 on November 11, still close to its 52-week high of $283.25.
bull: Caplyta passed its second big final-stage bipolar test, and J&J plans to use both tests to ask US regulators for approval.
J&J led a $100 million investment in Delix Therapeutics and is backing Francis Medical's prostate cancer device, adding new possible products.
The stock is trading near its 52-week high of $283.25, showing investors have been upbeat.
bear: A law firm said on November 12 it is looking into whether J&J misled investors, which is only an investigation but can bring lawsuits.
Third-quarter profit fell to just $210 million (9 cents a share) because of billions in costs to settle talc baby powder lawsuits.
Medical device sales grew only 2.5% last quarter, slowed by lower prices in China and trouble in the Middle East.

briefs.headline: MGM bounces back from a weak summer as a big shareholder buys $52 million more
briefs.summary: MGM Resorts runs casinos and hotels in Las Vegas, other US cities and Macau in China. Its results for July to September, shared on October 28, were weak: total sales of $4.2 billion slipped 1%, and its Las Vegas profit fell 12% because hotel room prices were lower. But the stock jumped about 4% on October 29 because the company said October business in Las Vegas bounced back, and a big shareholder, Barry Diller's group, agreed to cap its stake at 29.9%. After the results, funds run by MGM board member Keith Meister bought about $51.7 million of shares around $29 to $30 each, raising their stake by about 33%.
bull: MGM's CEO said Las Vegas business bounced back in October after a slow summer.
MGM China had record sales of $1.1 billion, up 5%, and its biggest share ever of the Macau market at 17.1%.
A board member's funds bought about $51.7 million of stock, a sign that insiders believe in the company.
bear: Las Vegas Strip profit fell 12% from a year ago because hotel rooms sold for lower prices.
MGM lost 11 cents per share last quarter on an adjusted basis (ignoring one-time items), compared with a 24 cent profit a year earlier.
The stock is down about 22% this year and about 44% below its May high of $50.69.

briefs.summary: On Friday, November 13, the Dow rose about 50 points, or 0.1%, to 52,347.55, the only major index to end higher. The Dow follows 30 big, well-known companies and holds fewer chip stocks, so the chip sell-off hurt it less as investors moved money into other kinds of companies. Dow member Nvidia still fell about 2% after its CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and Cisco dropped early even after a strong quarter. The Dow gained about 2% for the week.

briefs.headline: Small companies dip 0.3% Friday as interest rates climb above 5%
briefs.summary: On Friday, November 13, the Russell 2000, which tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies, fell about 0.3% to 2,790.49. It opened down about 1.7% before cutting most of its loss. Smaller companies often borrow more money, so they are hurt when interest rates rise, and the 10-year Treasury rate touched about 5.17% as traders bet on a Fed rate hike in December. This came after a 1.7% drop on Thursday, when small companies fell more than the other big indexes.

bear: The 10-year Treasury rate hit about 5.17%, raising borrowing costs for small companies.
